script: One drop of rain hits the sidewalk and suddenly your dog plants their feet and refuses to take another step, like the ground itself has become the enemy. Wet paws are actually a bigger deal to dogs than most owners realize. Their paw pads are packed with nerve endings, way more sensitive than we tend to assume, so an unfamiliar wet or cold texture underfoot can genuinely feel strange or uncomfortable in a way dry ground never does. Some of it is pure sensory dislike, but a lot of it is also learned, if a dog has ever slipped on a wet surface, gotten a paw uncomfortably cold, or just never built up positive experience with water on their feet as a puppy, that hesitation tends to stick around into adulthood. Breed and coat type play a role too, dogs with less natural water tolerance tend to be more dramatic about it than water-loving breeds. It's rarely stubbornness, it's closer to genuine discomfort meeting a bit of learned caution. A little positive exposure, treats, patience, and letting them approach puddles on their own terms usually helps far more than pulling them through it.
